preview.pick: She died in 1958 at the age of thirty-seven.

served.stem: According to the passage, each of the following is true of Rosalind Franklin EXCEPT:
choices: She trained as a physical chemist at Cambridge.
She spent three years in Paris learning X-ray methods.
She moved to Birkbeck College and worked on viruses.
She died in 1958 at the age of thirty-seven.
She shared the 1962 Nobel Prize with Wilkins.
served.bankWhy: Paragraph 10 says the 1962 prize went to Watson, Crick, and Wilkins, and that Franklin, who had died in 1958, could not have been included. The other four statements come from paragraphs 5 and 10.

proof.quote: Trained as a physical chemist at Cambridge
she had spent three years in Paris learning to apply X-ray methods
left for Birkbeck College in London, where she turned to the structure of viruses
She died of ovarian cancer in April 1958, at the age of thirty-seven.
the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine went to Watson, Crick, and Wilkins

steps: Flip the job. Four choices are in the passage; you are hunting the one that is not.
Check off two in paragraph 5, sentence 4: a physical chemist trained at Cambridge, three years in Paris.
Check off two in paragraph 10: Birkbeck and viruses, then her death in 1958 at thirty-seven.
The one left standing is the prize. Sentence 6 gives it to Watson, Crick and Wilkins.
